# arith_multiplier: specification to evidence

<!-- Generated by `python -m flow.trace_v1 write` (brief 116) from verif/testplan.yaml and the evidence files it names. Do not edit. -->

The human specifies the requirements and checks that the verification is thorough enough. The agent holds the knowledge to implement and to verify. You can open any of the implementation or the evidence, and you do not have to. Hardware on the board, with attached instruments, is a verification layer of its own: where a requirement depends on something outside the design (an optical link, a network card, a data source) it may be the only way to close it.

**Summary.** 9 requirements (9 functional); 1 verified; 6 partially verified (the required mix of methods is not met); 0 of 9 requirements agreed by a human, 0 agreed on the owner's delegation (not human), 9 draft; 6 resting only on the implementing agent's own tests; 0 human and 0 delegated review(s) recorded; 2 Lean proof item(s) (all widths): 0 with a human-approved statement, 0 with a statement accepted on the owner's delegation (not a human approval), 2 with statement not approved; 2 kernel only, 0 using a compiled decision procedure; build status from: recorded build (not re-run).

Arithmetic library, function multiplier (brief 139a). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

## Matrix

Rows are requirements, columns are verification methods. A cell lists each item with its computed status and links to its evidence. Status is read from the evidence by code; it is never typed. `stale` means a file the evidence is about changed after the evidence was recorded; `bounded` means a formal bounded model check only. A requirement is verified only when its passing items meet the method mix for its kind (`flow/method_mix_policy.yaml`); a test is marked with who wrote it, and a test whose author is not recorded counts as the implementing agent's own. Agreement comes only from `verif/agreements.yaml`, never from the testplan.

## Requirements in full

### MUL-F-MODEL: The bit-exact model is right

- Kind: functional; state: partially verified; lacks a simulation check from a bench the implementing agent did not write; rests only on the implementing agent's own tests; agreement: draft.
- Source: `arith/multiplier/spec.md`
- arith/multiplier/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a shift-and-add formulation (and, for the Booth recoding, the digit-sum identity)) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
  - simulation test: **pass**, The model against independent formulations (exhaustive small, random large) and the pinned conventions: 5 test(s) passed in the recorded run. [evidence](results/pytest_junit.xml)

### MUL-F-EXACT: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

- Kind: functional; state: partially verified; lacks a simulation check from a bench the implementing agent did not write; rests only on the implementing agent's own tests; agreement: draft.
- Source: `arith/multiplier/spec.md`
- At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (24 exhaustive points, 14 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.
  - simulation test: **pass**, Every variant against the model, every input, at the small points (Icarus + cocotb): 24 test(s) passed in the recorded run. [evidence](results/pytest_junit.xml)
  - simulation test: **pass**, Every variant against the model at the large points: edge values, carry runs and random inputs (Icarus + cocotb): 14 test(s) passed in the recorded run. [evidence](results/pytest_junit.xml)

### MUL-F-LAT: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

- Kind: functional; state: partially verified; lacks a simulation check from a bench the implementing agent did not write; rests only on the implementing agent's own tests; agreement: draft.
- Source: `arith/multiplier/spec.md`
- Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (dsp: STAGES; lut_array: REG; booth_r4: REG), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
  - simulation test: **pass**, The bench passes at the stated latency and fails two clocks off, for every variant: 3 test(s) passed in the recorded run. [evidence](results/pytest_junit.xml)

### MUL-F-EQUIV: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow

- Kind: functional; state: verified; agreement: draft.
- Source: `arith/multiplier/formal/jobs.yaml`
- SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.
  - formal: **pass**, k-induction proofs of the variants against the reference (4 jobs; widths in formal/jobs.yaml): 4 test(s) passed in the recorded run. [evidence](results/pytest_junit.xml)
  - formal: **pass**, Each formal check refutes a planted fault (the check can fail): 2 test(s) passed in the recorded run. [evidence](results/pytest_junit.xml)

### MUL-F-BENCH: The bench catches seeded faults

- Kind: functional; state: partially verified; lacks a simulation check from a bench the implementing agent did not write; rests only on the implementing agent's own tests; agreement: draft.
- Source: `arith/multiplier/verif/mutants.yaml`
- Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
  - simulation test: **pass**, The mutation run as a test: no mutant survives, none fails to build: 1 test(s) passed in the recorded run. [evidence](results/pytest_junit.xml)
  - simulation measurement: **pass**, Mutants killed of valid mutants (the record of the last full run): survived = []; invalid = []; valid = 17; score_pct = 100. [evidence](results/mutation.json)

### MUL-F-HARNESS: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

- Kind: functional; state: partially verified; lacks a simulation check from a bench the implementing agent did not write; rests only on the implementing agent's own tests; agreement: draft.
- Source: `arith/multiplier/harness/README.md`
- arith/multiplier/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
  - simulation test: **pass**, The packaged harness run standalone on every variant (with the checker and the coverage targets) and on a planted fault: 8 test(s) passed in the recorded run. [evidence](results/pytest_junit.xml)

### MUL-F-PACKAGE: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

- Kind: functional; state: partially verified; lacks a simulation check from a bench the implementing agent did not write; rests only on the implementing agent's own tests; agreement: draft.
- Source: `arith/multiplier/spec.yaml`
- spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
  - simulation test: **pass**, spec.yaml against the RTL headers, spec.md against spec.yaml, Verilator -Wall at every point, wrappers and build.yaml current and lint-clean: 5 test(s) passed in the recorded run. [evidence](results/pytest_junit.xml)

### MUL-F-LEAN-BOOTH: Radix-4 Booth digits sum to the multiplier's value, for every width

- Kind: functional; state: proved, statement not approved; agreement: draft.
- Source: `arith/multiplier/rtl/mult_booth_r4.sv (WBX, NP, bwide, bxe, the digit case table)`
- For every multiplier width, the radix-4 Booth digits d_i = -2 b[2i+1] + b[2i] + b[2i-1] of an even-length bit pattern sum, weighted by 4^i, to its two's-complement value. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
  - Lean proof (all widths): **statement not approved**, Radix-4 Booth digits sum to the multiplier's value: statement not approved; ArithBooth.booth_correct: kernel only; proof of the transcription, transcription not tested; recorded build (not re-run). [evidence](../../../formal/lean/records/build_record.json)

### MUL-F-LEAN-BOOTH-UNS: An unsigned multiplier extended by a zero bit has non-negative digits summing to its value, for every width

- Kind: functional; state: proved, statement not approved; agreement: draft.
- Source: `arith/multiplier/rtl/mult_booth_r4.sv (WBX, NP, bwide, bxe)`
- For every pattern whose top bit is 0 (an unsigned multiplier given the RTL's extra zero bit), the Booth digit sum equals the unsigned value. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
  - Lean proof (all widths): **statement not approved**, An unsigned multiplier extended by a zero bit has non-negative digits summing to its value: statement not approved; ArithBooth.booth_unsigned: kernel only; proof of the transcription, transcription not tested; recorded build (not re-run). [evidence](../../../formal/lean/records/build_record.json)
